motivation: The voltage difference is defined as Supply Voltage minus Capacitor Voltage: ΔV = Vs - Vc. An increase in supply voltage directly causes an increase in the voltage difference across the resistor, assuming capacitor voltage is constant.

Since Voltage Difference = Supply Voltage - Capacitor Voltage, an increase in capacitor voltage directly causes a decrease in the voltage difference. This is Kirchhoff's Voltage Law applied to the RC circuit.
According to Ohm's Law (V = IR), the current through a resistor is directly proportional to the voltage across it: I = ΔV/R. An increase in voltage difference causes an increase in current.
Ohm's Law states I = V/R. Current is inversely proportional to resistance. An increase in resistance causes a decrease in current for a given voltage difference.

By definition, current is the rate of charge flow: I = dQ/dt. The charging rate of the capacitor equals the current flowing into it. An increase in current directly causes an increase in charging rate.
This is a stock-flow relationship. Charge accumulates on the capacitor at the charging rate: Q(t) = ∫I dt. An increase in charging rate causes an increase in stored charge over time.
The fundamental capacitor equation relates charge to voltage: Q = CV, or V = Q/C. An increase in stored charge directly causes an increase in capacitor voltage (for constant capacitance).
